title: A little structure. A clearer day.
intro: You do not need a perfect routine. Start with one part of your life and two or three activities.
shots: Sign in with an email code
why: RoutineOS separates deciding from doing. Set up the reusable parts once, prepare a specific day, then follow it without rebuilding your schedule.
steps: Sign in
Enter your email, request a code, then enter the six-digit code from your inbox.
Start in Library
Create an area, then a routine. Videos are optional; ordinary tasks work too.
Prepare and follow a day
Use Plan to choose outcomes, then lock the day. Today becomes your next-step screen.
example: Study is an AREA. My Weekday is a ROUTINE. Finish lesson 3 is part of today's PLAN. TODAY tells you when to do it.
next: Start with Areas on the next page.

title: Give each priority a home.
intro: An area is simply a name and color for a part of your life. It is not another task to complete.
why: Areas keep related activities and learning resources together. You can recognize Study, Work or Training at a glance instead of reading an unorganized list.
steps: Create an area
Open Library > Areas, tap New, choose a short name and a color, then save.
Use it in activities
When making a routine, assign each activity to the area it belongs to.
Add resources if useful
Attach videos or playlists to an area. You can keep multiple courses in the same area.
example: Create Study in blue. Put DSA practice and JavaScript learning in Study. Both can use different courses without needing separate areas.
next: Next: give these activities times in a routine.

title: Build a day you can reuse.
intro: A routine is a reusable schedule. An activity block is just one thing to do, with a start and end time.
why: If your weekdays look similar, you should not have to enter the same schedule every morning. A routine supplies the shape; Plan adds that day's specifics.
steps: Name it and choose weekdays
Open Library > Routines > New. Use a name like My Weekday and select the days it fits.
Add activity blocks
Set each title, time and area. Choose a default course when relevant, then save the routine.
Reuse or adapt
Copy another routine when making a variation. Edit routines for future plans; an already locked day stays fixed.
example: My Weekday: 9-10 Study, 10-11 Work, 5-6 Training. A Weekend routine can have a different start time and fewer activities.
next: Next: add optional learning videos, or go straight to Plan.

title: Turn a long course into next steps.
intro: Keep your courses with their area, then choose only the lessons you need for a particular activity.
shots: A long video split into chunks
why: A saved link is easy to forget. A lesson attached to a planned activity gives you a specific place to continue, without hunting through tabs.
steps: Add a YouTube link
Open Library > Videos > Add. Select an area and paste a public video or playlist link.
Load the lessons
Load the video information. For a long video, choose a chunk length; browse playlists as individual lessons.
Choose what belongs today
In Plan, choose the course and select its lessons or chunks. An area can contain several playlists and videos.
example: Add a three-hour SQL video to Study. Split it into 30-minute chunks. Select the first chunk for today's study block; choose the next one when planning another day.
next: Videos are optional. Gym, errands and work blocks do not need them.

title: Decide what a good day looks like.
intro: A routine gives you the times. A plan adds the output, notes and chosen lessons for one particular day.
shots: Select a routine and prepare a block
Review activities and finalize the day
why: Study is vague. Finish one lesson and solve two questions tells you what done means. Planning that detail now reduces decisions later.
steps: Check the date and routine
If today is unplanned, Plan prepares today; otherwise tomorrow. Check the weekday-matched routine or select another.
Make each activity specific
Choose videos, write the output and add helpful notes. Finalize each block. Change titles, times and areas in the routine.
Review, then lock
Review the activity count and planned hours. Complete the confirmation steps to lock the day and send it to Today.
example: Output: finish SQL chunk 1 and write five examples. Notes: use the practice database. Video: the first 30 minutes of the SQL course.
next: Leave room for meals and rest. The 18-hour cap is a limit, not a target.

title: Follow the day, one activity at a time.
intro: This is your execution screen: the current activity, what comes next, and an honest record of what happened.
why: You already made the decisions in Plan. Today keeps the next action visible so you can spend your attention on doing it.
steps: Start with the current activity
Check the active block and its time. If the day is empty, tap Plan Today to prepare it first.
Open Details when needed
Tap the activity or Details to see the full output, notes and selected video links. A video count keeps the main card compact.
Record what happened
Mark done or skipped, and undo a mark if needed. After all activities are done, you can export the day's PDF report.
example: At 9:00, open Study, read your five-example output and play the chosen SQL chunk. Mark it done when finished. A missed activity does not erase the rest of your day.
next: No streak to protect. Make the record useful, not perfect.

title: Remember the errand when you arrive.
intro: Locations are saved places. Reminders are the things you want to do at those places.
shots: Reminders: tasks attached to a place
why: A shopping note cannot help if you forget to open it. An arrival reminder can bring the task back when you are near its saved place.
steps: Save a place
In Locations, tap Add location. Search, select a point on the map or use your position. Check the pin, name and radius, then save.
Attach the task
In Reminders, add what you need to do and choose the saved place. Several tasks can belong to one location.
Arrive, do it, tick it off
Allow notifications and background location in Settings. Unfinished tasks stay attached; repeat nudges are requested while you remain inside.
example: Save your supermarket, then add Buy milk. When arrival is detected, you get a nudge. Tick it off after buying it. Repeats stop after completion or a detected exit.
next: Android can delay detection and repeats. Reopen after Force stop; review location and battery settings.

title: Make it yours. Keep your work safe.
intro: Choose how the app looks, how it alerts you and when to check your backup.
why: The right permissions make reminders useful. A recent backup protects the routines and plans you have already spent time building.
steps: Choose your preferences
Set a name and photo, choose light or dark, and adjust notification sound and the start/end alert offsets.
Set up the reminders you use
Allow notifications for alerts. Arrival reminders also need background location. Follow the Android setup guidance for your phone.
Check your backup
Automatic backup runs every five minutes while online and active. Use Back Up Now before changing phones or uninstalling.
example: Prefer a heads-up? Set the start alert to 10 minutes before a block. Before replacing your phone, run Back Up Now and check its time, then sign in on the new phone.
next: Saved data works locally. Cloud restore and push need internet. One active device is allowed per account.
